data.title: Installed Building Products wins Buy rating at Stifel on housing recovery, M&A
data.description:
Stifel on Tuesday initiated coverage of Installed Building Products (IBP) with a Buy rating, citing the insulation installer’s resilient revenue, strong margins and acquisition opportunities.

Installed Building Products operates more than 250 U.S. branches and is the country’s second-largest residential insulation installer behind QXO (QXO). New residential construction accounts for 73% of installed revenue, followed by commercial construction at 20% and residential repair and remodeling at 7%.

For investors, Stifel’s thesis hinges on IBP weathering the housing downturn until residential construction improves. The firm also sees acquisitions, share repurchases and dividends supporting returns while investors wait. IBP shares had fallen 28% this year through Sept. 11, compared with an 11.9% gain for the S&P 500.

The company’s same-branch revenue increased 0.8% from 2022 through the 12 months ended in the second quarter of 2026, according to Stifel. That compares with a 4% decline in U.S. housing completions and a 6.6% drop in organic revenue among building-products distributors. IBP’s EBITDA margin expanded by 58 basis points to 17%, about 550 basis points above its peer group.

Stifel forecasts revenue rising from $3.01 billion in 2026 to $3.15 billion in 2027 and $3.32 billion in 2028. Adjusted earnings are projected to increase from $10.69 a share in 2026 to $11.79 in 2027 and $13.01 in 2028, representing a two-year compound annual growth rate of 10.3%.

Acquisitions remain another part of the bullish case. IBP has completed more than 100 purchases since its 2014 initial public offering, adding over $1.2 billion in annual revenue. Stifel estimated that M&A could add nearly 11 percentage points to shareholder returns during the next two and a half years if IBP deploys its available cash flow and balance-sheet capacity.

Risks include elevated interest rates, weaker housing demand, labor constraints, customer concentration and inflation in insulation products. Stifel also warned that aggressive behavior from IBP’s largest competitor and a shift away from higher-priced spray-foam insulation could weigh on its outlook.

Stifel's price target of $240 represents about 17% upside from IBP’s Sept. 11 closing price of $204.28. Analyst W. Andrew Carter based the valuation on slightly more than 13 times estimated 2027 EBITDA, assuming the stock regains a larger premium over building-products distribution peers.

data.title: agilon health upgraded at Bernstein on turnaround progress
data.description:
• Bernstein upgraded agilon health (AGL) to outperform from market-perform, saying that that a turnaround is producing positive results.
  • The firm boosted its price target to $125 from $86 (~35% upside based on Sept. 14 close).
  • Recent evidence of the turnaround is that in Q2, adjusted EBITDA was $70M compared to a loss of $83M in the year-ago period, according to analyst Lance Wilkes.
  • He sees adjusted EBITDA of $79M (company is projecting $85M) in 2026, $124M in 2027, and $160M in 2028.
  • "AGL has prioritized profitability over growth by repricing contracts, reducing risk exposure, and controlling operating costs," Wilkes wrote. "The company has reduced MA membership from 527k to 426k and cut Part D exposure from 70% of its book in 2024 to 15%, contributing to significantly lower [medical loss ratio]."

data.title: Magnificent Seven eyes a potential breakout after a sideways 2026
data.description:
A technical setup in the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) is drawing attention as traders watch whether mega-cap technology leadership can reassert itself.

Shares were recently changing hands near $69.75, just beneath a well-defined ceiling that has capped the fund through much of 2026. 

The equal-weight vehicle, which holds Alphabet (GOOG)(GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA) and Tesla (TSLA), oversees about $4.42B in assets. After years of outsized influence on major indexes, the group has spent this year largely range-bound. MAGS is up roughly 5.6% year to date, trailing the S&P 500’s (SP500) gain of about 10.2%. 

Chart technicians point to repeated tests of resistance in the low-$70s, a pattern some describe as an ascending triangle approaching resolution. A decisive move above that band—particularly through the recent $70.80 high—could reopen upside for the Nasdaq 100 and large-cap growth stocks that still dominate market capitalization.

Because these seven names remain a heavy component of broad benchmarks, a MAGS breakout would not be isolated. It would signal that the same cohort that powered prior advances is again absorbing selling and attracting bids. Failure to clear the zone would keep the 2026 sideways narrative intact and leave leadership with the rest of the market. Investors will watch volume and follow-through in the sessions ahead.

data.title: Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo surge as merger enters final stages
data.description:
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) and Qorvo (QRVO) shares surged during Tuesday trading as the proposed merger between the two semiconductor companies nears completion.

Qorvo climbed 7% while Skyworks soared 10%.

"We are very confident that we're going to close this calendar year," said Skyworks CEO Philip Brace during a Goldman Sachs conference last week. "We're preparing to close this fiscal year."

Skyworks' fiscal year ends on September 30. The two companies have already cleared a review by U.S. antitrust regulators. The deal is in the final phase of being reviewed by China's State Administration for Market Regulation, which is the last hurdle before the merger can close.

"This company coming together really does two things," Brace said. "It has a scale play and a diversification play. And the scale play really gets us significantly more revenue, and then we're able to really financially do $500M of synergies, which we get there. So we should have, I think, around a roughly $5.5B mobile business and then a $2.5B, $2.6B nonmobile business."

Brace explained how the two companies merging allow them to build more for the handset market and enter new markets, such as the defense industry.

"Like if we just look at the handset side today, right, Qorvo, the product lines are barely overlapping, right?" Brace said. "They have antenna tuning, envelope tracking and PMIC. We don't have any of those technologies. And so when you think from the receiver all the way to the antenna, you might believe that bringing in thousands of RF engineers might allow us to do things differently. And we know there are certain customers today, where we have 100% of the RF front end, and we know we can do things differently. So I'm excited about that opportunity."

Skyworks and Qorvo first announced the proposed merger in October 2025.

data.title: Wells Fargo CFO expects 2026 loan growth to be better than previously guided
data.description:
Wells Fargo (WFC) CFO Michael Santomassimo expects 2026 loan growth to be better than what was previously guided.

Santomassimo was speaking at the Barclays 24th Annual Global Financial Services Conference.

Talking about the loan environment, the CFO said activity was good. Growth was up 12% in the first half, while the management had guided mid-single-digit year-over-year growth by the fourth quarter.

"While we'll likely be better than where we guided in the first part of the year, it will be a little bit lower than what that 12% number, certainly for the full year," he said.

"But, I think that will set us up well as we go into next year. Activity levels are still pretty good."

"The last couple of quarters, loans are a little bit better than we thought," he told analysts, noting that good client acquisition at the commercial bank is helping drive loan growth.

data.title: History shows that rising yields hurt stocks only when growth weakens
data.description:
A look at more than five decades of data indicates that climbing Treasury yields do not automatically pressure stocks. What matters is the growth backdrop that accompanies the move.

The U.S. 10-year yield (US10Y) has recently topped 5%, renewing a familiar debate among investors. A long-run study isolates only those months in which the 10-year was rising and then splits the sample by whether economic growth was strengthening or fading. The resulting paths of S&P 500 (SP500) excess returns, shown on a log scale from 1970 through mid-September 2026, diverge sharply. 

When growth was accelerating, equities generated substantial cumulative excess returns even as yields advanced, finishing near +200%. When growth was deteriorating, the identical rising-yield environment produced a steep, persistent drag that left excess returns around -150%. The blended series of all rising-yield months sits in between and ends only modestly positive. 

The historical record clearly shows higher yields have been a meaningful headwind for stocks mainly when they coincided with weakening growth. In expansionary periods, equities have often absorbed the rate increase and continued to advance. That distinction offers a useful filter as markets digest a 5% 10-year and assess the current growth impulse.

data.title: Generation Mining secures C$340M final funding for Marathon project in Ontario
data.description:
Generation Mining (GENMF) said Tuesday it secured C$340M in final funding to complete a fully financed C$1.3B construction package for its 100%-owned, fully permitted Marathon copper-palladium project in Ontario.

Canada Growth Fund said it committed to invest C$140M in Generation Mining (GENMF) through $90M in the company's common shares as part of a broader C$200M equity financing and a C$50M convertible note as part of a C$100M offering of convertible notes to be issued by Generation on a private placement basis.

The Marathon project is expected to produce 2.1M oz of palladium, 532M lbs of copper, 488K oz of platinum, 160K of gold, and 3M oz of silver over its 13-year lifetime.

Canada Growth Fund is "playing a catalytic role in the project's financing structure... and its investment is a cornerstone for the Marathon project and has been instrumental in unlocking the broader capital required to move the project forward," Generation Mining (GENMF) CEO Jamie Levy said.

data.title: Fed hike may not be hawkish enough for markets, Brooks says
data.description:
The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise interest rates this week, but the bigger market test could come from what Chair Kevin Warsh says afterward as investors look for clues on how far the central bank is prepared to tighten.

Markets are pricing a 25-basis-point hike at this week's meeting, with another quarter-point increase priced by December and two more expected in 2027, according to Robin J. Brooks. The gap between those expectations and what the Fed signals could determine the market reaction.

The Fed will release its policy statement and updated economic projections at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday, followed by Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. Brooks expects the dot plot to point to one more rate increase this year, rather than the more aggressive path currently reflected in markets.

That could leave Warsh facing pressure to explain whether the Fed intends to deliver the additional tightening investors are anticipating. Brooks expects the central bank to raise rates but for Warsh's comments to fall short of those expectations, creating what he described as a "dovish hike."

Such an outcome would likely push the dollar lower while lifting gold and the S&P 500, according to Brooks. He also expects the Treasury yield curve to steepen as markets reassess how much additional tightening is actually coming.

The more bullish outcome for the dollar would be a hike accompanied by a clearly hawkish message that validates current market pricing. Brooks sees that scenario as unlikely. He also views a no-hike decision as problematic because it could damage confidence in the Fed's credibility, even if Warsh subsequently delivered a hawkish message.

At the other extreme, a combination of no hike and a dovish press conference would likely send the dollar sharply lower while boosting gold and equities, but Brooks also considers that outcome unlikely.

Brooks said the broader policy objective is to keep longer-term Treasury yields anchored through a new relationship between the Fed and Treasury. But he warned that the strategy could run into trouble if Wednesday's press conference leaves markets believing the Fed is less hawkish than the tightening path already priced in.

data.title: Meta launches Meta One subscription service across its apps
data.description:
Meta (META) on Tuesday said it is rolling out a new subscription service, Meta One, that gives users expanded access to artificial intelligence tools and additional features across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Meta AI.

Plans for this service are now available globally, starting at $2.99 a month for individual products, $7.99 for individual bundles, and $14.99 for creator and business bundles. This includes more than 50 features at launch, with plans to expand to Edits and AI glasses over time. Meta (META) said its core apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions provide additional AI usage and specialized capabilities.

For individual users, the company offers single-product subscriptions as well as Core and Premium bundles. The latter provides greater access to AI-powered image and video generation, as well as tools such as Instagram’s Restyle. Meta (META) said more than half of subscribers in early testing used both AI and expression features in its bundled plans.

Meta (META) is also offering subscription tiers for creators and businesses, with tools including enhanced profiles, content scheduling, analytics, and greater access to Meta Business Agent for customer responses.

Business and creator plans range from Essential, starting at $14.99 a month, to Max, starting at $499 a month. The Facebook parent said pricing and available features may vary by region, app, and account.

The company said its individual single-product plans, including Instagram Plus, Facebook Plus, and WhatsApp Plus, have shown strong retention as the company continues to expand them.

data.title: Telix climbs for second trading day following Pixclara approval
data.description:
• Telix Pharmaceuticals (TLX) is up ~11% in Tuesday trading as the stock continues to benefit from the recent US FDA approval of Pixclara (floretyrosine F 18), a radioactive diagnostic drug used to help evaluate patients with brain cancer.
  • On Monday, shares closed up ~4%.
  • Pixclara is the first FDA-approved FET-PET imaging agent for glioma.
  • Speaking at the Morgan Stanley Global Healthcare Conference in New York on Monday, Telix CEO Christian Behrenbruch called Pixclara a platform, adding there is considerable potential for other indications. "We have currently other clinical activity running to expand the label over time…," he said, adding that TLX-101, a therapeutic, is in phase 3 for glioblastoma multiforme.
  • "We've got some really exciting clinical data around that program," Behrenbruch said. "And so the imaging and the therapy is really very complementary, and one de-risks the other."
